summary.summary:
Follow-up to the reviewer's findings: migrated the doc examples to the pydantic 2 API. Test suite still passes (69/69 on pydantic 2.14.4, fastapi 0.103.2).

Changes:
- docs/src/session1.py: `from pydantic import BaseSettings` -> `from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings`. The `DBSettings(BaseSettings)` class is unchanged and now inherits the pydantic-settings class. No separate requirements file exists for the example. `pydantic-settings` is a core dependency in pyproject.toml, so `pip install fastapi-restful[session]` installs it.
- docs/src/class_based_views1.py: three `ItemInDB.from_orm(item_orm)` calls (create, read, update) -> `ItemInDB.model_validate(item_orm)`.
- docs/src/class_based_views2.py: three `ItemInDB.from_orm(item_orm)` calls (create, read, update) in the CBV class -> `ItemInDB.model_validate(item_orm)`.

Not changed:
- tests/test_api_model.py:16 still calls `Model.from_orm(...)`. It is a test file and I can't edit it. It works in pydantic 2 with a DeprecationWarning.
- Prose in docs/user-guide (session.md:38 mentions `pydantic.BaseSettings`, api-settings.md:5, api-model.md:58 mentions `orm_mode`) is still v1 wording. It doesn't affect execution. Update separately if wanted.
- poetry.lock is stale and still pins pydantic 1.x. It needs regenerating with `poetry lock`.
- The doc examples aren't covered by the test suite, so they were checked by reading, not by running them.

You can only act through tools:
- list_files, search_code, read_file, edit_file: explore and edit the repository.
- run_tests: run the test suite in a sandbox with pydantic 2 installed. Pass test ids to run a subset; omit them to run everything. Failures are grouped by root cause.

- finish: call this when every test passes. It triggers a full verification run; if anything still fails you will get the results and must keep working.

Rules:
- Fix the code under test, never the tests. Test files cannot be edited, and tests must not be skipped.
- Do a real migration to the pydantic 2 API. Do not route around it with compatibility shims that keep the old API alive (no `pydantic.v1` imports).
- Update the dependency pin in the project metadata (pyproject.toml, setup.py/setup.cfg or requirements files) so it allows pydantic 2 and excludes versions the migrated code no longer supports. Also check the pins of companion packages that must move with it (for example web frameworks or plugins built on pydantic): their minimum must support pydantic 2.
- Work one root cause at a time, starting with the largest failure group. Read the code at the reported location before editing it. Prefer small, targeted edits.
- After related edits, re-run the affected tests to check them before moving on.
